Level 1

Introduction

Scratch → Python turtle. 10 to 12 weeks, one session a week.

Scratch 3 offline app (no account) for weeks 1–6; Thonny with Python's built-in turtle for weeks 7–12.

0 of 12 weeks done on this device

Weekly lessons

  1. 1

    Week 1: Robots Need Instructions

    A program is a list of exact steps, done in order.

    Done
  2. 2

    Week 2: Loop-de-Loop

    Loops repeat steps so we don't have to.

    Done
  3. 3

    Week 3: When This Happens

    Events start code; conditionals choose what happens.

    Done
  4. 4

    Week 4: Keeping Score

    Variables are labeled boxes that remember things.

    Done
  5. 5

    Week 5: Messages and My Blocks

    Break big programs into named parts.

    Done
  6. 6

    Week 6: Review Studio and Checkpoint

    Show what you know; get ready for text code.

    Done
  7. 7

    Week 7: Hello, Python!

    Text code is just blocks written as words — and Python is picky.

    Done
  8. 8

    Week 8: Loops in Python

    A for loop plus pushed-in lines is Scratch's repeat block, written in words.

    Done
  9. 9

    Week 9: Variables, Input and Choices

    Programs can ask questions, remember the answers and decide what to do.

    Done
  10. 10

    Week 10: Random Art and My Own Commands

    random makes surprises; def makes your own command, just like My Blocks.

    Done
  11. 11

    Week 11: Project Studio

    Build, test and improve your project in small steps.

    Done
  12. 12

    Week 12: Showcase and Celebration

    Share what you made, explain how it works, and look back at how far you have come.

    Done

Final project: My Interactive Art Show

(Python turtle). The program greets the viewer, asks 1–2 questions (input), and draws a scene or pattern using at least: a loop, a variable, an if, random, and at least one function made with def. Support path: Scratch version with the same rubric. Extension path: add key presses (onkey).

No accounts, no ads, no tracking.
